steps.content: Knock knock knock...
Come in.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Chief, we've finished sorting the info on Sinner Lamia. After going through all the posts and rumors online, this is what we've got.
Nightingale hands you a folder. When you open it, there are only two pieces of paper inside.
One is her basic bio. The other is half a page of personal info unrelated to her role as "Ocean Messenger."
...That's all?

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Yeah. Sorry, Chief. Repeated investigations by the intelligence department yielded the same results.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: Lamia's "Ocean Messenger" identity has covered up a lot about her own identity.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: While the President of the Thaumas Society primed Lamia, he deleted a lot of information about her, and even altered her appearance for their livestreams. The technical department is trying to restore some of the data, but it will take time.
Okay, got it.
Then please arrange an interrogation in two days. It seems that we must learn about her past, including her involvement with the Thaumas Society, in her own words.
You see Lamia flinching visibly the moment the light turns on. She sneaks a glance at you and her voice trembles, just like when you first met her.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...Chief? What am I doing here?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: It's so dark and scary here... Did something happen? Is that why you brought me here...
Her eyes are downcast and full of worry, but not for herself—instead, she seems to be worried about the potential trouble you're facing.
Don't be scared, Lamia. You've behaved quite well since coming to the MBCC. You haven't violated any rules, and everyone has spoken highly about you.
I'm just here for a routine inquiry. I want to know some details about the Thaumas Society.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...Really? I'm glad I didn't cause trouble for you guys.
She sighs in relief and unknits her brows, revealing a faint smile.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: So, what do you want to know, Chief? I'll make sure to help you as much as I can.
I've been curious about the Thaumas Society since arriving to Ogygia Villa. What kind of organization is it?
You've been tracking this organization online and suspect that Sinners are involved, but it's too strictly guarded. Even if you pay to become a member, the chance of meeting a core member is slim.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ah... are you interested in becoming a Seafarer? We are a maritime culture research organization. We facilitate the exchange of ideas between ocean enthusiasts.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: All life originated from the ocean, so we believe it is the cradle of all souls. The deep sea is spiritual and wise, and holds the immense power to purify and enlighten.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: In addition, we believe there is another world at the bottom of the sea, where life that remained in the ocean gained intelligence and established their own civilization.
I've read that already on your homepage. I want to ask about the things not available to the general public.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: What do you mean?
For example... your offline gatherings?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ah, you mean our in-person meetings?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Yes, the President regularly invites our most dedicated fans, as well as those with unique insights into maritime culture, to meet with me at Ogygia Villa. It's an opportunity to exchange ideas and explore the mysteries of the world together.
Just to exchange ideas?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Yes... why do you ask?
She fidgets in her chair, and her eyes dart about. It's evident that she's hiding something, and... lying.
Speaking of the "President," what kind of person is he? How is your relationship with him?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: The President... is a very good person. I've always felt grateful towards him. He is patient and kind, and takes care of everyone, including myself. Anyone who has attended our meetings has more or less experienced that. So...
She clasps her hands over her chest and flashes a faint smile.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: We all admire the President. I pray every day that he gets the ocean's blessings that he yearns for.
So, you don't know... that he died in Ogygia Villa?
Your question seems to shock Lamia.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Wh-what?! The President... he...!!
We found a corpse in Ogygia Villa. The MBCC's autopsy confirmed it to be the President of the Thaumas Society.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: How could this be... He... He said that we'd go back to the Society together after dinner...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I... I was still worrying about missing that meeting... How could the President have... ended up in the sea...
Lamia lowers her head even more, resting her chin on her clasped hands. Tears brim in her eyes and tremble on her eyelashes.
So... you knew nothing about this?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: W-what's that supposed to mean? Of course I don't know anything about this! Surely you don't think I have something to do with this!

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I was with you and Miss Cabernet when it happened, remember?

test

test
You're a lousy liar, Miss Lamia.
You put the autopsy report on the table and push it towards Lamia.
I don't think you understood what I meant by "the MBCC's autopsy."
What happened in Ogygia Villa was a Mania incident, so all the evidence went through the MBCC's lab. We have evidence to prove that he died from a poisonous, hallucination-inducing Sinner's power.
The autopsy report completely blows her cover. She's now fully aware that there's solid evidence against her.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ah... Chief, I... it's not what you think! I-I really didn't want to, but I had no choice... Please trust me!
Stuttering in defense, she looks pleadingly at you with tearful eyes, as if you're her last hope for survival.
No choice? Why?
As if wanting to say something but hesitant and afraid to, Lamia lowers her head and clasps tightly onto the armrests.

options: Ask her to tell the truth

choices.text: Ask her to tell the truth

steps.content: You lean in close to her, softening your tone.
The people who planned that banquet will all be investigated and punished. If you hide anything from us, we might consider you to be an accomplice.
So... if you keep hiding the truth, I can't help you.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...All right, I'll tell you.
Biting her lip, she finally makes up her mind and starts to talk:

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Like I said before, I've always truly respected, appreciated and depended on the President.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: After all, when a freak like me came to this wholly unfamiliar world, had nowhere to go and almost starved to death on the streets, he was the one who took me in.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: The President gave me a place to stay, and made me realize that I, too, had the worth to keep on living.
"Wholly unfamiliar world"...?
Her odd wording makes you frown, but you continue to listen without interrupting.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: He helped me come to terms with my skin color. He also taught me how to comfort those driven to desperation by this cruel world at in-person meetings, so that they may rekindle their hope and passion for life...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: In fact, I often feel that the Seafarers and I are each other's saviors. I heal their wounds, while they make me feel accepted and loved.
...So this is the truth of your in-person meetings? You use your power to comfort them?

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...No. This is what I thought was the truth.
Lamia shakes her head, smiling bitterly.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I wish I hadn't passed by the President's room that night. I wish I hadn't eavesdropped out of curiosity. Perhaps then I could've continued to live in my dream, and all those bad things wouldn't have happened.
Lamia curls up in her chair, seeming to recall a very painful scene.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: But in reality, he didn't do any of those things for the sake of those poor, tormented Seafarers. It was all for greed and money. I was just a tool... a puppet he used to trick others...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: It wasn't till that night that I found out everyone had to pay him a hefty "membership fee" to join my in-person meetings.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Those poor, desperate Seafarers sought me for comfort because of how much they suffered.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Yet the President exploited their pain and suffering for money. That's not something I can accept.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I didn't want to go to that banquet and participate in his scams anymore... We had an argument in the Ogygia Villa's control room... He said there were plenty of others who'll do what I won't...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: He said there weren't that many honorable souls in this world, and that I could be replaced at any moment. He even decided to abandon me on the spot and kill me.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I was so scared that I lost control... I swear, I really didn't mean to, I just wanted to live...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I truly wanted to relieve the Seafarers' suffering. I truly wanted to help them, but ended up helping the President harm them instead.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Maybe I'm just destined to be a monster who brings disaster to those around me... It was all an illusion. I didn't attain salvation, nor could I save others.
Lamia's voice is so full of pain and guilt that you can't help but feel moved.
Based on previous investigations, you know that such organizations are usually scams. They took in a desperate soul like Lamia and exploited her power to scam others.
All you can do is try to uproot such organizations and save one Lamia after another.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Sorry, Chief. I choked up a bit. How embarrassing.
As you ponder how to comfort her, she wipes the corners of her eyes and flashes you a grateful smile.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I've always been the one listening to others' troubles... It's my first time confessing my own troubles to someone else... It feels so good. Thank you for listening to me.

Sorry for bringing up these awful memories, but it's a routine procedure. Thank you for cooperating. I now have a general understanding of the Thaumas Society. I have one last question before wrapping up our interrogation today.
Perhaps surprised by how quickly the interrogation is ending, her expression becomes a bit off, but she quickly fixes it.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Of course... Ask away.
You mentioned just now that "the President took you in"... That was indeed the case. We found an old nurse and learned some things from her. Perhaps... it's related to your past.
You put a voice recording pen on the table. Lamia stares at it with a grim look on her face.
If what she says is true, and you want to pursue the matter... we can offer you help.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Is the past... of particular importance to the Bureau? I joined the Society at an early age. I don't remember what happened before then.

Lamia is being overtly resistant, making you puzzled as well as troubled. But you need to get to know her better—you hope that after leaving Thaumas, she can learn to survive without using her power or trickery.
Sorry. The Bureau's top psychiatrist will be right at the door. I will immediately stop the recording if you feel unwell... But I still hope that you can confirm its content.

Lamia nods lightly, and you start to play the recording. Amidst the rustling static, an elderly voice begins to speak.

steps.speaker: Old Nurse
steps.content: My my, how could I forget such a special child? I've been a midwife for decades and delivered thousands of babies, but I've never seen anything quite like her.

steps.speaker: Old Nurse
steps.content: That child was as gray as ash when she was born. Quite the bad omen! The doctors and nurses were all shocked. Even the mother screamed and fainted when she saw the child.

steps.speaker: Old Nurse
steps.content: Moreover, I heard that the mother died of illness not long after. Nobody dared to adopt that monstrous-looking child. They kicked her around like a ball for quite some time, until some distant relatives were pressured to take her in.

steps.speaker: Old Nurse
steps.content: I don't know what happened after that. The child was illegitimate to begin with, so her relatives took her from the hospital without filling in the proper papers. They didn't leave any information with us.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: I... I don't remember... I really don't remember...
Lamia mutters to herself as pain and panic creeps onto her face.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: ...Don't hurt me... Let me go... Let me go...
She begins to tremble uncontrollably, curling up into a fetal position. Her eyes lose focus and her breathing speeds up as she mutters incomprehensibly.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Ah!!!
Lamia lets out a piteous scream. You quickly stop the recording and cast your shackles to stabilize Lamia.
Lamia, don't be scared. You're safe and sound in the MBCC. No one will hurt you here...
After a long silence, Lamia finally calms down.
Let's call it a day. Go back and get some rest.
You did well... I pushed you too hard. I didn't mean any harm. I just wanted to help you.
As you get up to lead her out, she suddenly grabs the corner of your shirt.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Eastside Psychiatric Hospital
...What?
As if making a difficult decision, she takes a deep breath and looks up at you again.

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Eastside Psychiatric Hospital. That's where you can find out about... my "past."

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: You're right. Only by knowing this will you be able to help me...

steps.speaker: Lamia
steps.content: Help me, Chief.
